thread:
maria.support: FYI customer AcmeFin is seeing requests routed to hosted despite having a VPC/dedicated pin for eu-west-1. High latencies (~600ms) and some 503s, plus a billing spike. Can someone pick this up? :urgent:

alex.eng-runtime: On it. Can you paste a sample request + any routing headers / trace ids?

maria.support: here's a sanitized curl from their app (they're hitting our API gateway):

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-***" \
  -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Pin: eu-west-1:d-42" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","prompt":"test"}'
```

Response: `503 Service Unavailable` with body `{"error":"backend_unavailable","pool":"hosted-eu-3"}`.

Also from their logs we see intermittent `401`/`403` auth errors that map to our hosted pool auth layer (weird). Billing shows many requests counted against hosted host-pool.

chen.eng-infra: Hmm—control-plane routing logs for that pin id show a recent pin refresh job restarted at 1952344000. There is a gap where the pin TTL was extended client-side but the control plane worker briefly re-registered with older metadata. I can pull the routing decisions.

alex.eng-runtime: Can you paste the routing trace for a failing request (x-request-id)? Want to see policy eval and fallback decision. If fallback->hosted happened, we need to know which condition triggered (capacity, auth, region mismatch).

maria.support: sample trace id: rq_0a7b9cde. Log excerpt:

```
[1952345560] route_eval: pin_lookup -> found pin:d-42 (eu-west-1)
[1952345560] pool_select: dedicated_pool:d-42 -> checkout failed (evicted)
[1952345560] fallback_policy: allow_hosted -> selected hosted-eu-3
[1952345560] auth_forward: token routed to hosted auth proxy -> auth 401
[1952345560] request_completed: 503 backend_unavailable
```

tim.eng-sre: That `checkout failed (evicted)` line is important. Eviction could be transient (OOM / preempt) but we shouldn't send traffic to hosted if auth/region mismatch risk exists. Do we have a recent change to fallback semantics?

chen.eng-infra: We deployed a change (1952345000) to speed up eviction detection: if a pool reports <10% free slots, it's marked for soft-evict and traffic is allowed to fallback. I suspect the threshold was too aggressive for pinned pools with small capacity.

ingrid.product: This is exactly the thing customers call out — pinned capacity should never fallback to hosted without an explicit allow_fallback flag on the customer's account. AcmeFin uses dedicated for compliance. Fallback caused both latency and billing surprises. We need immediate mitigation and a policy change.

alex.eng-runtime: Short-term mitigation options:
- toggle `allow_hosted_fallback=false` for AcmeFin in routing table (fast, per-account override)
- increase soft-evict threshold so small pools aren't marked evictable so quickly
- for auth: ensure that when we fallback we do not drop to the hosted auth namespace (preserve account-level auth routing)

maria.support: Can someone flip the per-account override? Customer is hitting support and asking for an ETA.

tim.eng-sre: I can flip the flag. Doing `PATCH /internal/routing/accounts/acme_firm -d '{"allow_hosted_fallback":false}'` now.

infra-bot: deploy started by tim.eng-sre: routing-config-update v1.12.3 -> v1.12.4 (1952345880)

tim.eng-sre: Done — we set allow_hosted_fallback=false and invalidated the routing cache for that account. Please confirm from the customer's side.

maria.support: Customer confirms immediate drop in latency; no further 503s in last 3 minutes. They still saw some billing counts against hosted for earlier requests and want a credit.

ingrid.product: We should offer a credit and notify finance. Also need a policy change: pinned dedicated pools should default to no-hosted-fallback unless customer opts in. Add to next week's roadmap.

chen.eng-infra: For root cause: sequence was — quick pin TTL refresh race + aggressive soft-evict threshold caused temporary mark of dedicated pool as evicted -> routing allowed hosted fallback -> auth tokens forwarded to hosted auth namespace (different verifier) -> 401/403 and hosted billing. I'll open a postmortem with timeline and repro.

alex.eng-runtime: Repro steps I used locally (please run on staging to validate):
1) create small dedicated pool (2 slots) and pin account to it.
2) run heavy parallel warmup to reduce available slots: `ab -n 200 -c 40` against model endpoint to trigger soft-evict condition.
3) concurrently trigger a pin TTL refresh (simulate control plane restart) to create a short mismatch window.
4) observe routing logs show `checkout failed -> fallback host` and hosted auth path.

```
# example: simulate traffic
wrk -t8 -c60 -d30s https://staging-api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-test'
```

tim.eng-sre: Action items:
- chen: roll back or tune soft-evict threshold and add guard for pinned pools (low capacity pools shouldn't be auto-evicted)
- alex: change fallback to preserve auth namespace / add strict check for account-level allow_hosted_fallback flag before forwarding tokens to hosted auth
- ingrid: customer comms + billing credit request to finance
- maria: keep monitoring AcmeFin for 24h and confirm no cross-billing

chen.eng-infra: I'll also add a canary test that simulates pin refresh during heavy load to catch this in CI.

maria.support: Thanks all. Marking as escalated to SEV-2 for now. I'll update the ticket with the mitigation and ETA for the fix. :white_check_mark:

alex.eng-runtime: Noted. I'll follow up with a patch for auth-preservation and unit tests.

infra-bot: deploy successful: routing-config-update v1.12.4 (1952346010)

maria.support: Closing slack thread; will attach postmortem link when ready.
